capabilityRows.notes: Alibaba mirrors upstream 2.0.76: `ALIBABA_API_KEY`, versioned user-agent suffix, chat/language callable aliases, DashScope chat completions with thinking/reasoning mapping, generated fallback IDs for missing tool-call IDs, cache-aware usage with nonnegative reasoning-adjusted output text tokens, historical assistant reasoning omission including removal of reasoning-only turns, DashScope embedding endpoint with dense and sparse option mapping, video submit/poll flow, wan2.6 legacy video protocol, wan2.7 media/ratio video protocol, WAN 3 all-in-one media/resolution/aspect-ratio/audio mapping and usage metadata, provider option validation, warnings, provider metadata, and unsupported image families. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 2026-09-20 pass adds typed `preserveThinking`, model-aware defaults, and assistant reasoning-history replay. The 2026-09-27 pass adds model-aware Qwen 3.7/3.8 JSON Schema routing and preserves unsupported-structured-output warnings for other model families. The 2026-10-11 pass: Common max reasoning uses a 95 percent token budget; embedding dimensions default from the shared request and provider dimension overrides it. The 2026-10-18 pass: Wan video routing parses numeric versions: pre-2.7 IDs retain legacy requests, later 2.x IDs use the Wan 2.7 tiered protocol, and 3+ or unknown future IDs use the current all-in-one media protocol. The 2026-10-23 pass: Polling and status resource IDs are encoded as one path segment, including reserved characters and standalone dots.

Amazon Bedrock Converse, embeddings, images, and reranking mirror upstream 5.0.124: SigV4 and bearer auth, versioned user-agent suffix, Converse request/stream parsing, ordered generated content with signature, legacy redacted-data, and current redacted-content replay metadata, event-stream decode/process failure propagation and incomplete-frame EOF rejection, empty tool-call ID normalization, provider options under `amazonBedrock`/`bedrock`, service tiers, guardrails, top-level reasoning mapping, cache points, Converse inline and S3 video sources across ten supported MIME types, document citations, rich tool-result content, strict-tool warnings and JSON response fallback that preserves ordinary tools, Cohere batch embeddings up to 96 inputs, Nova/Titan/Cohere embedding response shapes, and the current `bedrockRerankingConfiguration` rerank request key. The latest pass omits assistant turns left empty after unsigned-reasoning filtering, and also preserves exact case-sensitive `s3://` image sources in user and tool-result content, sanitizes replayed tool names, percent-encodes ARN model paths, and omits strict/native structured-output fields for Claude families that Bedrock rejects. The 5.0.68 pass also adds inference-profile reasoning, cache-only assistant omission, ARN embedding-family detection, citations, parallel-tool disabling, guardrail block handling, complete raw usage, model-specific reasoning shapes, and typed stream errors. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, optional JS headers config, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 5.0.76 delta adds `structuredOutputMode`, separate native-output and strict-tool model gates including Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5, sibling-safe `output_config` filtering, citation-nested text extraction, sanitized document names, and alternating user turns for replayed provider-executed tool results. The 2026-09-20 pass adds opaque Anthropic-family settings, recursive strict-schema validation, current web-tool warnings/bindings, and non-2xx stream error parity. The 2026-09-27 pass adds current model capability gates, forced-tool and sampling rules, reasoning normalization, Claude Opus 5.5 and Mistral ID handling, and Mantle routing; Swift still cannot distinguish omitted from explicitly empty `stopSequences`. The 2026-10-04 pass passes string requestMetadata, omits Nova 2 Lite maxTokens for high thinking, validates generated region hosts, and reports Nova Canvas image-input capabilities. The 2026-10-11 pass: Claude Haiku 5.5 capability gates, explicit disabled thinking, max reasoning and embedding dimensions follow the published baseline. SigV4 omits non-ASCII header values from the signed set while retaining outgoing headers. The 2026-10-18 pass: Recognizable supported Claude generations receive strict/native-output fields; unknown Claude IDs use conservative prompt JSON instructions in automatic mode. Non-Claude and opaque inference profiles retain their prior behavior.

Bedrock Anthropic mirrors upstream 5.0.124 invoke-model behavior: Anthropic Messages request conversion, Bedrock auth and user-agent handling, URL/data media resolution, native Anthropic tool helpers, model-specific structured-output and strict-tool omissions, event-stream decoding that surfaces decode/process failures and rejects incomplete frames at EOF, response metadata, and Bedrock-specific request URLs. JS fetch/header injection hooks remain JS-only. The 5.0.76 pass shares the new structured-output mode selection, model capability gates, document sanitization, citation extraction, and provider-executed tool-result replay. The 2026-09-27 pass inherits current Claude capability, tool-choice, sampling, and reasoning gates. The 2026-10-18 pass: The shared Messages implementation carries attached citations, separates retrieved web sources, and preserves tools under none/manual-thinking tool choices.

Bedrock Mantle mirrors upstream 5.0.124 chat and responses surfaces with Bedrock Mantle hostnames, SigV4 or bearer auth, OpenAI-compatible request builders, versioned user-agent suffix, and provider metadata. JavaScript module-format exports are not applicable in Swift. The 2026-09-27 pass aligns model-family routing and current Responses behavior.

Anthropic mirrors upstream 4.0.88 across Messages, files, and skills: thinking, citations, cache control, hosted/provider-defined tools, streamed code-execution input subtypes, `fallbacks: default` beta routing, caller metadata replay for client/server tools and web-search results across generated and streamed responses, Claude Opus 5 and forward-compatible Claude capabilities, structured-output tool safeguards, reasoning-token usage details, and provider metadata. Advisor tools map per-inference `maxTokens` and replay `stopReason`; stream parsing rejects spliced message IDs while tolerating duplicate starts for the active message; code-execution transcripts retain their complete prompt-cache-compatible wire shape. Generic adaptive reasoning requests include `display: summarized`. Generated response blocks retain upstream order across reasoning, text, citations, sources, tool calls/results, and compaction; signed/redacted thinking and text citation metadata are preserved. Mid-conversation system-message `toolChanges` map to tool-addition/removal content blocks with automatic beta headers, while initial-system changes warn and are ignored; toolChanges-only empty text does not consume an invisible cache breakpoint. `thinking: disabled` is forwarded and incompatible `xhigh`/`max` effort is lowered with a warning. Files and skills clients add the required Anthropic beta headers. The language wrapper also implements durable Batch V4 start/status/result streaming with strict response validation, redirect-safe JSONL retrieval, per-item terminal failures, and programmatic deferred-result replay without leaking the internal discriminator. Current Batch parity forwards the full request setting/content surface, preserves native counts and raw status, isolates invalid or unknown result items, safely encodes returned skill identifiers, and warns because completion webhooks are unsupported. The 4.0.49 delta adds Fable 5.1 and Vertex Claude 4 recognition, mid-conversation `clearAt` and `effort`, updated adaptive display and binding-only thinking behavior, plus the context-management, structured-outputs, interleaved-thinking, and web-search beta headers. Streaming multipart file bodies remain JS-specific because the Swift file client accepts buffered `Data`. The 2026-09-20 pass adds the 20260318 web tools and deferred lifecycle, normalizes implicit code execution, preserves custom aliases, and exposes a Messages-backed Evaluation V4 adapter. The 2026-09-27 pass adds Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 recognition, `computerToolset_20260801`, current structured-output safeguards, and compaction, toolset, and effort behavior. The 2026-10-04 pass adds Sonnet 5.5 between_tools thinking, replayable native fallback markers, historical missing-caller normalization, and lossless toolset action replay. The 2026-10-11 pass: Claude Haiku 5.5 adaptive thinking, sampling, structured output and effort behavior is recognized; message_start provider metadata is retained. Batch downloads accept a positive maxLineBytes limit, defaulting to 64 MiB. The 2026-10-18 pass: Text blocks and stream endings expose normalized citations while retaining complete raw provider citation metadata. Retrieved web results remain independent sources with citation fallback only when retrieval is absent. Manual thinking downgrades forced tools; none preserves tool definitions. Tool-result file references and tool-search error/cache replay follow the current Messages protocol. The 2026-10-23 pass: Compatible Messages configuration supports provider-specific media/cache/sampling behavior; batch beta options reject explicit null. The 2026-10-25 pass: Nonempty unfinished Messages output reports interrupted; explicit provider stops/errors retain their mapped semantics and metadata.

Anthropic AWS mirrors upstream 2.0.81 request signing, regional endpoint handling, and the shared Anthropic Messages behavior represented by the Swift provider. JavaScript AWS credential-provider hooks remain runtime-specific. The 2.0.41 pass inherits the shared Anthropic 4.0.49 system-option, thinking, model-recognition, and beta-header behavior through AWS signing. The 2026-09-27 delta is version-identity-only and continues to inherit shared Anthropic behavior. Generated-host regions are validated as complete single DNS labels; custom endpoints bypass unused region validation. The 2026-10-11 pass: Inherits current Messages/Haiku behavior; non-ASCII headers remain outgoing but are excluded from SigV4 signing. The 2026-10-18 pass: Shared Messages citation, thinking/tool-choice and tool-result file-reference behavior follows the current Anthropic adapter, including the native AWS provider-reference namespace.

AssemblyAI transcription mirrors upstream 3.0.68: `ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY`, custom headers, versioned user-agent suffix, `transcription`/`transcriptionModel` aliases, `/v2/upload` plus `/v2/transcript` submit/poll flow, legacy `best` via `speech_model`, current `universal-3-5-pro`/`universal-3-pro`/`universal-2` via `speech_models`, deprecation and migration warnings, providerOptions.assemblyai schema including Universal 3 Pro and GA nested options, millisecond-to-second word segment conversion, audio-intelligence provider metadata, raw final response metadata, AssemblyAI error schema, and unsupported language/embedding/image families. ProviderV4, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns.

Azure OpenAI mirrors upstream 4.0.110: `AZURE_API_KEY` or per-request Microsoft Entra token provider auth, `AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME`, versioned user-agent suffix, Responses as default callable/language surface, chat/deepseek/completion/embedding/textEmbedding/image/transcription/speech aliases, Azure provider metadata namespace, deployment-based transcription URLs, Azure OpenAI base URLs with `/v1` and `api-version`, custom non-Azure gateway base URLs used as-is, DeepSeek reasoning mapping without thinking support, OpenAI option namespace mapping, Azure content-filter placeholder metadata suppression, and Azure-specific hosted tool helpers. The 4.0.63 pass normalizes Azure OpenAI, Foundry, Cognitive Services, custom gateway, deployment, and `/v1` URL shapes without duplicating `/v1` or `api-version`, and inherits the shared OpenAI GPT-6 request behavior. Files V4 remains exposed by the OpenAI and xAI file clients. The 2026-09-27 pass inherits strict-false function tools and validated, positioned GPT-6 reasoning-effort updates from the shared OpenAI Responses path. The 2026-10-04 pass adds MAI Voice 2/2.1 and Flash Speech synthesis with SSML/style/voice/format handling, MAI Transcribe 1.5/2 file transcription with timed phrase metadata, and MAI Transcribe 2 streaming over an injectable cancellable WebSocket. AzureOpenAIAudioSettings configures separate Speech/MAI base URLs. Entra auth applies to both audio hosts; generated resource names must be single DNS labels. Azure image file/mask capabilities are unknown. The 2026-10-11 pass: MAI Image supports generation and image editing, multiple references and grouped results, API-key or Entra auth, and native error handling; the OpenAI image path remains available. The 2026-10-18 pass: Current Responses citations/history/additional-tool behavior is inherited. webSearchPreview is deprecated in favor of webSearch. The 2026-10-23 pass: Per-model AzureOpenAILanguageModelSettings separates model identity/capability gates from deployment routing for Responses, chat and completion. The 2026-10-25 pass: Inherits OpenAI final-answer JSON selection and interrupted stream completion while retaining deployment/model identity separation.

Chat and embedding endpoints mirror upstream Baseten 2.1.56: `BASETEN_API_KEY`, versioned user-agent suffix, custom Model API base URL, `/sync/v1` chat model URLs, `/sync` or `/sync/v1` embedding model URLs, OpenAI-compatible HTTP embedding bodies/options with 128-input batching, native JSON Schema structured output enabled by default, streamed chat usage enabled by default, unsupported image models, and both string and nested OpenAI-shaped `error` envelope parsing. The optional native NAPI performance client is JavaScript-specific.

Black Forest Labs image and FLUX 3 video generation mirror upstream 2.0.70: `BFL_API_KEY`, `x-key` auth, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, `image`/`imageModel` and `video`/`videoModel` aliases, `black-forest-labs.image` and `black-forest-labs.video` provider IDs, `/v1/{model}` submit URLs, response-supplied polling with trusted `bfl.ai` sibling-host credential forwarding, signed result URLs, provider options and warnings, response/provider metadata, and structured errors. Video supports text-to-video, first/last/timed keyframes, continuation, draft generation/enhancement, and settled cost metadata. Unary generation remains source compatible; `AsyncVideoModel` adds serializable V4 start/status operations, stable idempotent start retries, and shared facade polling. BFL has no native webhook, so a supplied webhook warns and falls back to polling. Language and embedding families remain unsupported. The 2026-09-20 pass enforces wall-clock image polling deadlines that can abort a hung request. File/mask image capabilities are now exposed as async Bool? getters; unrecognized models remain unknown. The 2026-10-11 pass: FLUX 3 Image supports reference images, grounded prompts, resolution/ratio/seed mapping, terminal failure parsing and credential-isolated result downloads. The 2026-10-18 pass: Latest and future image IDs use the current model-specific submit protocol with file inputs, dimension/ratio/resolution controls and safetyTolerance up to 7; known legacy IDs retain their original protocols.

ByteDance Seedance video models mirror upstream ByteDance 2.0.71: `ARK_API_KEY`, versioned user-agent suffix, current Dreamina/Seedance model IDs, prompt/image/frameImages/inputReferences mapping, standard unary generation plus public AsyncVideoModel start/status operations, provider options for watermark/camera/returnLastFrame/serviceTier/draft/reference media/polling, resolution mapping, warnings, polling/error metadata including returned last-frame URLs, and unsupported non-video families. Upstream image-token usage has no local analogue because this provider exposes video only. Status polling now follows only validated redirects and never forwards credentials away from the configured origin. The 2026-09-20 pass emits `reference_image` when a start image is combined with additional references.

Cartesia REST speech, batch transcription, and Ink 2 streaming transcription mirror upstream 3.0.63: `CARTESIA_API_KEY`, Bearer auth, `Cartesia-Version` default `2026-03-01`, custom headers and Swift base-URL override, versioned user-agent suffix, speech/transcription aliases, `/tts/bytes` JSON speech, `/stt` multipart batch transcription, and `/access-token` plus duplex `/stt/turns/websocket` or `/stt/websocket` streaming. Streaming supports raw PCM/G.711 encodings, server turn detection or explicit finalization, partial/final events, raw chunks, token-redacted metadata, cancellation, and an injectable `AIDuplexWebSocketTransport`. Full realtime speech-session generation remains a broader protocol gap; `ink-2` batch calls still fail locally before network I/O. The 2026-10-18 pass: Only ink-whisper and dated ink-whisper-* IDs are batch-only. Other current and future IDs use the existing duplex transcription protocol.

Cerebras chat models mirror upstream Cerebras 3.0.78: `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, custom base URL and headers, callable provider plus `languageModel`/`chat` aliases, `cerebras.chat` provider IDs, versioned user-agent suffix, typed provider-option validation, `maxOutputTokens` mapped to `max_completion_tokens`, current model IDs such as `gpt-oss-120b` and `qwen-3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507`, structured outputs, reasoning transform, structured-output tool-call normalization, flat Cerebras error schema, empty tool-call ID normalization, and unsupported embedding/image families.

Cohere mirrors upstream 4.0.69: `COHERE_API_KEY`, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, callable/language aliases, embedding/textEmbedding aliases, reranking aliases, chat `/v2/chat`, embedding `/v2/embed`, reranking `/v2/rerank`, prompt conversion for text/images/documents/tool calls, providerOptions.cohere schemas, top-level reasoning to Cohere `thinking` budget mapping, providerOptions thinking precedence, response format and tool choice mapping, streaming lifecycle/tool-call/reasoning parts, response metadata with complete raw usage, embedding/reranking response bodies, object-document reranking warnings, and unsupported non-text document media. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, TypeScript option export renames, optional JS headers config, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 2026-10-11 pass: Embeddings select float, int8, uint8, binary or ubinary responses, support 768/2048 dimensions and common-dimension defaults; chat retains cached token accounting.

Deepgram transcription and speech mirror upstream 3.1.39: `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`, `Token` auth, custom headers, versioned user-agent suffix, `transcription`/`transcriptionModel` and `speech`/`speechModel` aliases, `/v1/listen` raw-audio transcription with explicit-only diarization and providerOptions.deepgram query mapping, `/v1/speak` JSON TTS with output format to encoding/container/sample-rate mapping, Aura family plus voice/language model-ID composition, speech speed, incompatible audio cleanup and unsupported-instruction warnings, response-header usage/provider metadata, structured `err_code`/`err_msg` errors, and unsupported language/embedding/image families. ProviderV4, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, experimental streaming transcription types, optional JS headers config, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. Native seconds/characters audio usage is exposed without converting billing units into token counts.

DeepInfra mirrors upstream 3.0.78: `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY`, bearer auth, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, callable/chat/language aliases, completion/embedding/textEmbedding aliases, image/imageModel aliases, `deepinfra.chat`/`.completion`/`.embedding`/`.image` provider IDs, `/openai/*` language/embedding routes, `/inference/{model}` image generation, OpenAI-compatible multipart image edits, Gemma/Gemini reasoning usage correction, native JSON Schema structured output enabled by default, `providerOptions.deepinfra` passthrough, max-one generated image per call, and response metadata. File/mask image capabilities are now exposed as async Bool? getters; unrecognized models remain unknown.

DeepSeek chat models mirror upstream DeepSeek 3.0.73: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, custom base URL and headers, callable/language/chat aliases, `deepseek.chat` provider IDs, versioned user-agent suffix, reasoning/thinking mapping, providerOptions.deepseek thinking and reasoningEffort schema, cache-aware usage/provider metadata, JSON response instruction injection, generated fallback IDs for missing generate tool-call IDs, streaming response metadata, stream usage, OpenAI-compatible tool calls including strict mode, DeepSeek V4 assistant reasoning_content rules, V4 Flash Vision Exp inline, URL, and provider-reference images, Files V4 upload with `user_data`, expiry validation and structured errors, and unsupported embedding/image-generation families. The 3.0.37 pass also covered model-aware reasoning/sampling rules, log probabilities, user/message metadata, strict function-tool preparation, upload preflight and response metadata, complete usage, and typed stream failures. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 2026-09-20 pass aligns empty-choice failures with the exact upstream structural error. The 2026-09-27 pass preserves multimodal V4 and Flash tool-result text, provider references, URL and base64 images, and rejects unsupported image URL media types. Standard cached prompt-token details are used when provider-specific cache-hit counts are absent. The 2026-10-11 pass: Common xhigh and max reasoning both map to max; native file bytes already cover the published Blob type-only cleanup. The 2026-10-18 pass: Future DeepSeek models use the V4 protocol unless recognized as legacy chat/reasoner/R1/V3 identifiers.

ElevenLabs speech and transcription mirror upstream 3.0.71: `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `xi-api-key` auth, custom headers, versioned user-agent suffix, camel-case Swift `AIProviders.elevenLabs` factory, `speech`/`speechModel` and `transcription`/`transcriptionModel` aliases, speech `/v1/text-to-speech/{voice}` request builder with output format aliases, voice settings, pronunciation dictionaries, normalization options and warnings, transcription `/v1/speech-to-text` multipart builder with `scribe_v2`, providerOptions.elevenlabs defaults and schema validation, response text/language/segments/duration, response metadata, ElevenLabs error schema, and unsupported language/embedding/image families. SwiftAISDK additionally exposes locally ported ElevenLabs music, sound effects, voice changer, voice isolator, and dubbing helpers. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, optional JS headers config, TypeScript export split, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 2026-10-11 pass: Scribe response word metadata retains speaker and confidence evidence without altering the default diarize=true behavior. The 2026-10-25 pass: Native streaming speech accepts incremental text and v3/v4 dialogue with per-part voices/options, cancellation and typed failures. Unary speech routes dialogue, music and sound effects with validated native composition plans; reported transcription duration wins.

Fal image, transcription, speech, and video models mirror upstream Fal 3.0.69: `FAL_API_KEY`/`FAL_KEY`, `Key` auth, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, image/transcription/speech/video aliases, image `/fal.run/{model}` requests with file and mask data URI mapping, native speech generation plus unauthenticated audio download, queue-based transcription and video polling, same-origin credential forwarding for video response URLs, foreign response URL credential stripping, providerOptions.fal schemas and camelCase-to-snake_case mapping, deprecated image snake_case warnings, video `video/mp4` media type fallback, response/provider metadata, Fal error schema, and unsupported language/embedding families. Fal video additionally implements Async Video V4 start/status operations and native webhook registration; the shared facade splits requests by `maxVideosPerCall`, preserves stable idempotency, and can complete by webhook or polling while unary generation remains source compatible. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, TypeScript option export splits, optional JS headers config, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. File/mask image capabilities are now exposed as async Bool? getters; unrecognized models remain unknown. The 2026-10-23 pass: Polling and status resource IDs are encoded as one path segment, including reserved characters and standalone dots.

Fireworks mirrors upstream Fireworks 3.0.81: `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, bearer auth, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, callable/chat/language/completion/embedding/textEmbedding/image/imageModel aliases, chat/completion/embedding string and structured object error-envelope messages, native JSON Schema structured outputs, includeUsage streaming by default, current Kimi K2.6 and Minimax M2 model IDs, thinking/reasoningHistory/promptCacheKey/serviceTier mapping, reasoning_effort minimal/xhigh normalization, sync and async image endpoints, same-origin credential forwarding for async downloads, providerOptions.fireworks passthrough, warnings, and response metadata. ProviderV4, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 2026-09-20 pass enforces a wall-clock image polling deadline that aborts hung requests. File/mask image capabilities are now exposed as async Bool? getters; unrecognized models remain unknown. The 2026-10-11 pass: Common max effort maps to high through the shared chat helper.

Fish Audio mirrors upstream 3.0.46: `FISH_AUDIO_API_KEY`, bearer auth, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, binary `/v1/tts` speech generation with model headers, output formats, latency/normalization/sampling controls and warnings, plus multipart `/v1/asr` transcription with language, duration, and timed text segments. Request/response metadata, abort propagation, and Fish `{status,message}` error handling follow the published package.

Gateway mirrors upstream 4.0.126: default `/v4/ai` base URL, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`/`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` auth, team scoping, protocol/auth-method headers, versioned user-agent suffix, language/embedding/image/video/reranking/speech/transcription aliases, durable Batch V4 start/status/results with ordered mixed content, callback URL forwarding, reconciled nonnegative native request counts, typed `not_found` errors, Tako Search, async-video start/status and native callback registration, unary transcription plus duplex streaming transcription, and a callable experimental transcription factory that mints short-lived route-bound tokens. Gateway providerOptions cover BYOK, routing order/fallbacks, provider allow-lists, prompt-training restrictions, `has` filtering, sort, serviceTier, quota, and tags; response/provider metadata, model/credits/spend/generation APIs, retryable structured errors, and provider tools are retained. Full realtime model sessions, Vercel o11y headers, metadata-cache refresh policy, ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, and workflow serialization helpers remain JS/runtime-only gaps. The 2026-09-20 pass adds native Evaluation V4 models, catalog discovery, headers, abort propagation, result metadata, and structured error mapping. The 2026-09-27 pass adds Browserbase search and fetch tools, forward-compatible has filters, and provider-owned batch cancellation with lifecycle-status validation. Gateway 4.0.95 also validates conditional Evaluation V4 fallbacks and attributes results to the model that actually answered. The 2026-10-04 pass routes credits team IDs/slugs through query parameters, accepts all-question conditional evaluation fallback thresholds, and preserves native audio usage including stream finishes. The 2026-10-11 pass: Decision V4 uses /decision-model with normalized inline file evidence; batch JSONL downloads have a configurable 64 MiB default line limit. Shared embedding dimensions and missing xAI diarization evidence are handled. The 2026-10-23 pass: Decision requests forward optional maxOutputTokens and reasoning without adding absent defaults. The 2026-10-25 pass: Native streaming speech, speech-bound client secrets and interoperable WebSocket envelopes are available. Parallel Search supports GA modes, top-level maxCharsTotal, fetch timeout/cache policy and location; raw results preserve GA snake_case fields.

Gladia transcription mirrors upstream 3.0.68: `GLADIA_API_KEY`, `x-gladia-key` auth, custom headers, versioned user-agent suffix, `transcription`/`transcriptionModel` aliases, `/v2/upload` multipart audio upload, `/v2/pre-recorded` initiation, provider-supplied result polling with same-origin credential forwarding, foreign result URL credential stripping, providerOptions.gladia schema and snake_case mapping, result text/language/segments/duration, response/provider metadata, Gladia error schema, lifecycle errors, and unsupported language/embedding/image families. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, optional JS headers config, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns.

GMI Cloud chat mirrors upstream 3.0.49: `GMI_CLOUD_APIKEY`, bearer auth, custom base URL and headers, versioned user-agent suffix, callable/language/chat aliases, forward-compatible string model IDs, OpenAI-compatible chat streaming, usage enabled by default with unknown usage fields preserved, and nested JSON `error.details` unwrapping for actionable backend diagnostics. Embedding and image families remain unsupported.

Google Generative AI's implemented Gemini language, embedding, image, TTS speech, Veo video, files, interactions, and agents surface was audited against upstream Google 4.0.105. The current pass adds the published 100-input embedding preflight limit. Imagen factories remain locally available for source compatibility after their removal from the current upstream package. Gemini 3.7 Flash normalizes `none` and `minimal` reasoning to the supported `low` thinking floor. Primitive JSON Schema enum/const values and local `$ref` expansion, including boolean-schema references, map to Gemini's OpenAPI-compatible wire form, while strict forced/named tools use `ANY` and strict automatic tools retain `VALIDATED`. Interactions forwards topK and seed while warning for unsupported penalties and agent-dropped settings; Files resumable uploads leave payload length to the transport. Generate and stream results surface Gemini `responseId`; multiple code-execution results retain their originating call ID; parallel unsigned function calls reuse an earlier signed standard call; and unknown future Gemini IDs default to the newest supported tool, thinking, file-search, and multimodal response capabilities while known legacy families stay conservative. Speech maps Gemini TTS generateContent requests with WAV-wrapped PCM by default, raw PCM opt-in, multi-speaker provider options, response sample-rate metadata, and upstream warnings. Gemini 3.5 unary/live transcription, Files URL recognition, recursive-tool behavior, and Gemini 2.5 penalty warnings remain deferred to a dedicated provider pass. Realtime/WebSocket speech translation and lifecycle events and JS ProviderV4 runtime helpers also remain gaps. The 4.0.64 pass adds JSON Schema `minItems` and `maxItems`, preserves caller function aliases, forwards file headers and cancellation, supplies a durable Batch V4 adapter with tool content and input-file metadata, and supports Interactions video plus processing-call/result request, response, stream, warning, and metadata handling. Final integration also round-trips Interactions response history, function and built-in tool items, reasoning items, compaction state, provider references, `mediaResolution`, and `systemInstruction` precedence; Google Batch rejects empty result keys and preserves thought signatures even when their associated text is empty. The 2026-09-20 pass adds lossless schema conversion, corrected block reasons, accumulated stream metadata and usage, exact image-count behavior, custom provider names, and a Gemini-backed Evaluation V4 adapter. The 2026-09-27 pass adds embedding provider-option slicing, image metadata, video offsets, code-execution replay, JSON Schema `$ref` URIs, and current TTS behavior. The 2026-10-04 pass reports Gemini image file/mask capabilities and retains speech usageMetadata. Gemini transcription and Google Realtime remain deferred. The 2026-10-11 pass adds collision-safe JSON response tools with application tools, incremental nested JSON parsing and real-tool/signature preservation, Gemini 3 native automatic selection, shared embedding dimensions and Decision V4. Batch downloads default to a configurable 64 MiB UTF-8 line limit. The 2026-10-18 pass: GenerateContent auto-continues long decodes with cumulative output budgets, summed per-hop usage and initialPromptTokenCount metadata. Checkpoint tokens support explicit resume. AUDIO output, explicit thinking precedence, dotted route IDs and background Interactions polling are supported.

Vertex's implemented Gemini language, tuned endpoint, embedding, Gemini TTS speech, Cloud Speech-to-Text transcription, Veo video, and Interactions surface was audited against upstream Google Vertex 5.0.122. The current pass exposes the published embedding limits: 250 inputs for standard models and one input for Gemini multimodal embeddings. Imagen image generation/editing factories remain locally available for source compatibility after their removal from the current upstream package.
